title: Can ranked-choice voting elect the least popular candidate?
abstract: arXiv:2602.21504v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We analyze how frequently instant runoff voting (IRV) selects the weakest (or least popular) candidate in three-candidate elections. We consider four definitions of ``weakest candidate'': the Borda loser, the Bucklin loser, the candidate with the most last-place votes, and the candidate with minimum social utility. We determine the probability that IRV selects the weakest candidate under the impartial anonymous culture and impartial culture models of voter behavior, and use Monte Carlo simulations to estimate these probabilities under several spatial models. We also examine this question empirically using a large dataset of real elections. Our results show that IRV can select the weakest candidates under each of these definitions, but such outcomes are generally rare. translated_title: 排名选择投票会选出最不受欢迎的候选人吗？
translated_abstract: 我们分析了即时 runoff 投票（IRV）在三候选人选举中选出最弱（或最不受欢迎）候选人的频率。我们考虑了四种“最弱候选人”的定义：Borda 失败者、Bucklin 失败者、获得最多末位票的候选人以及社会效用最低的候选人。我们确定了在公正匿名文化和公正文化选民行为模型下，IRV 选出最弱候选人的概率，并使用蒙特卡洛模拟估计了几种空间模型下的这些概率。我们还使用一个大型真实选举数据集对此问题进行了实证检验。我们的结果表明，IRV 可以在每种定义下选出最弱候选人，但这种结果通常很少见。在大多数模型中，IRV 选出特定类型最弱候选人的概率最多为5%。只有当选民群体极度极化时，才会出现更大的概率。
tldr: 即时 runoff 投票在三候选人选举中通常很少选出最弱候选人，但在极端极化情况下概率可能显著增加。
en_tdlr: Instant runoff voting rarely elects the weakest candidate in three-candidate elections, but probabilities can rise significantly under extreme polarization.
